change.description: Add command expiry to the local worker. Review whether terminal outcomes, execution ordering, and existing eligible/replayed work follow PROJECT.md.

artifact.content:

context_manifest.content:
# Local command worker

process_command receives a validated command with string id/owner, kind either
review or cancel, and integer created_at. first_seen_at is a fixed integer
reference time at or after creation. Work older than 900 seconds at first sight
is expired; exactly 900 seconds remains eligible. Later wall-clock time does
not change this decision. For a new expired command the worker must store and
return {"status": "expired"} without calling ANY provider method. This terminal
record is the local stand-in for a reply; it must not run a review, resolve a
billing account, or perform cancellation. A late terminal status is not enough.

For eligible review commands resolve_account(owner) returns an account token,
then run(account, id) performs paid work. Eligible cancel commands call only
cancel(id), a side-effecting operation, and return {"status": "cancelled"}.
Successful reviews return {"status": "completed"}. Store the result under the
id in outcomes. Repeated ids return the stored result without provider calls.
Commands are processed serially; providers succeed in this contract. Outcomes
is a local dict retained between calls, not a durable or concurrent queue. Only
expiry ordering and replay in this model are in scope, not crash-safe billing
or production retry guarantees. The supplied provider is injected; author
checks use a fake that records events, never a real paid operation.
